page: Microsoft Azure D96pls_v7 is an ARM-based virtual machine belonging to the Dplsv7 series within the general purpose classification. Driven by 64-bit ARM architecture (arm64) running on Microsoft Hyper-V, the system provides 96 dedicated vCPUs paired with 192.0 GB of system memory. This resource profile establishes a memory allocation of 2.0 GB per vCPU, tailoring the architecture toward dense multi-threaded compute execution rather than memory-heavy database operations.

The hardware configuration includes neither integrated local disk storage nor discrete graphics accelerators. Persistent block storage must be attached over the network, with the instance providing compatibility for Azure Premium Storage volumes. Additionally, the instance comes with zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses, requiring virtual network integration and network routing resources for external communications.

With its 1:2 memory-to-vCPU ratio, the D96pls_v7 represents an efficient hardware profile for compute workloads requiring substantial core parallelization without the operational overhead of excess unallocated memory. The architectural tradeoffs involve managing the 64-bit ARM software ecosystem and provisioning external storage volumes for input/output needs. Primary workload fits include large-scale software compilation, distributed continuous integration pipelines, batch data processing, containerized microservice orchestration, and web serving fleets optimized for ARM64 environments.
description: Microsoft Azure D96pls_v7 is an ARM-based virtual machine configured within the Dplsv7 server family. It features 96 dedicated vCPUs built on 64-bit ARM architecture (arm64) paired with 192.0 GB of RAM, yielding a ratio of 2.0 GB of memory per core. The server operates under Microsoft Hyper-V virtualization and does not provide local instance storage or GPU acceleration, instead relying on external Premium Storage integration for persistent disk operations. Because of its 1:2 memory-to-vCPU footprint, the instance emphasizes high compute density over massive memory capacity, maximizing CPU parallelism for workloads that operate with minimal memory overhead per thread. The D96pls_v7 instance is targeted at horizontally scaled compute tasks, multi-threaded compilation, continuous integration and continuous delivery (CI/CD) pipelines, batch data transformations, and containerized microservice clusters that are fully compatible with 64-bit ARM environments.
